correctness.rationale: The canonical log-trace identity separates the coefficient of reciprocal time A_j, linear-time coefficient B and intercept ell_j. Three distinct post-onset positive times identify each triple by a degree-two interpolation. With known upstream sign, two sensor A_j ratios determine source and dispersion; the ell_j slope determines drift; B fixes decay; intercept fixes mass. Removing the side restriction admits the explicit geometry-changing q-transformation whose A_j,B,ell_j all coincide and whose k remains nonnegative. Three sensor A_j uniquely interpolate a quadratic to determine the source and dispersion globally. Exact mass equality follows by solving a strictly monotone exponential equality at the unique positive drift. All parameter boundaries D,v,M>0, k>=0 and noncoincident sensor location are retained. The on-disk standard-library checker replayed 4,215 assertions; these are diagnostic, not a substitute for the algebra.

An explicit physically admissible calibrated-mass alias shows why knowing release dose is not by itself a remedy, while a justified upstream prior reduces the requirement from three stations to two even with drift, dispersion and loss unknown.
